```{r setup}
library(adorn)
```

These examples use the `timed`, `logged` and `memoize` decorators from
`vignette("examples_01")`, repeated here so this vignette stands alone.

```{r timed}
timed <- decorator(
  function(f, ..., digits = 3) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    start <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
    on.exit(message(sprintf(
      "%s took %s s",
      name,
      round(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - start, digits)
    )))
    f(...)
  },
  name = "timed"
)

slow_add <- timed %@% function(x, y = 1) {
  Sys.sleep(0.1)
  x + y
}
slow_add(2)
```

```{r logged}
logged <- decorator(
  function(f, ...) {
    name <- decorator_context()$name
    message("-> ", name)
    result <- withVisible(f(...))
    message("<- ", name)
    if (result$visible) result$value else invisible(result$value)
  },
  name = "logged"
)

double <- logged %@% function(x) x * 2
double(21)
```

```{r memoize}
memoize <- decorator(
  function(f) {
    cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    function(...) {
      key <- paste(deparse(list(...)), collapse = "")
      if (!exists(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)) {
        assign(key, f(...), envir = cache)
      }
      get(key, envir = cache, inherits = FALSE)
    }
  },
  name = "memoize"
)

fib <- memoize %@% function(n) if (n < 2) n else fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
fib(30)
```

# Decorating S3, S4, S7 and R6 methods

`%@%` works wherever you define a function, so it can decorate a method as you
write it. For a method that already exists, use `decorate()`. The examples
below use the `logged`, `timed` and `memoize` decorators defined above.

## S3

```{r s3}
money <- function(x) structure(list(amount = x), class = "money")

print.money <- logged %@% function(x, ...) {
  cat("$", format(x$amount, nsmall = 2), "\n")
  invisible(x)
}

print(money(12.5))
```

To decorate an existing method, give `decorate()` the generic's name as a
string and the class:

```{r s3-decorate}
format.money <- function(x, ...) paste0("$", x$amount)
decorate("format", timed, class = "money")

format(money(3))
```

## S4

```{r s4}
setClass("Circle", representation(r = "numeric"))
setGeneric("area", function(shape, ...) standardGeneric("area"))

setMethod("area", "Circle", logged %@% function(shape, ...) pi * shape@r^2)

area(new("Circle", r = 2))
```

Decorate an existing method by giving `decorate()` the generic and the
signature. Calling it again adds another layer on the outside, and
`decorators()` lists the stack, outermost first.

```{r s4-decorate}
setClass("Square", representation(side = "numeric"))
setMethod("area", "Square", function(shape, ...) shape@side^2)

decorate(area, logged, signature = "Square")
decorate(area, timed, signature = "Square")

area(new("Square", side = 3))
decorators(getMethod("area", "Square"))
```

## S7

```{r s7}
library(S7)

Dog <- new_class("Dog", properties = list(name = class_character))

speak <- new_generic("speak", "x")
method(speak, Dog) <- logged %@% function(x) paste(x@name, "says woof")

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

Decorate an existing method with the generic and the class, or with the
replacement form, which mirrors `method(generic, class) <- fn`:

```{r s7-decorate}
decorate(speak, Dog) <- timed

speak(Dog(name = "Rex"))
```

## R6

Decorated methods keep access to `self` and `private`, and `invisible(self)`
still chains.

```{r r6, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
library(R6)

Counter <- R6Class("Counter",
  public = list(
    n = 0,
    add = logged %@% function(k = 1) {
      self$n <- self$n + k
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

counter <- Counter$new()
counter$add(2)$add(3)
counter$n
```

Decorators with state work too. R6 methods belong to the class, so the cache
below is shared by every `Model` object (the key is the argument, not `self`).

```{r r6-memoize, eval = requireNamespace("R6", quietly = TRUE)}
Model <- R6Class("Model", public = list(
  scale = 10,
  predict = memoize %@% function(x) {
    message("computing")
    x * self$scale
  }
))

m <- Model$new()
m$predict(2)
m$predict(2)
```

For an R6 class that already exists, use `decorate()` with the generator and the
method name; see `vignette("examples_03", "adorn")`.
